text: Sub: Regulation 30 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“Listing Regulations”) – clarification on news in mainstream media We write to you in relation to the news reports dated 4 th July, 2025 published in public domain, including NDTV article titled ‘ Ultratech Under Scanner In Cement Cartelisation Case’, which are false and misleading. It is clarified that the Company is not under investigation in this Case No. 35 of 2020 before the Competition Commission of India (“CCI”). The Company has neither received any order from the CCI in this case nor have the Company’s financials been sought by the CCI. UltraTech Cement reserves its rights to take necessary legal steps in light of these misleading reports to protect its reputation. The above is for your information and record.

text: Sub: News Clarification - "Reliance denies receiving Russian oil at its Jamnagar refinery in recent weeks” We refer to your letter / email dated January 6, 2026 seeking clarification on the news item - “Reliance denies receiving Russian oil at its Jamnagar refinery in recent weeks ”. In our view, there is no linkage between the movement in price of equity shares of the Company and captioned news article. We would like to clarify that despite the denial by the Company of buying of any Russian oil to be delivered in January , a news report was published in Bloomberg claiming ‘three vessels laden with Russian Oil are heading for Reliance Industries Limited’s Jamnagar refinery”. text: Sub: Intimation regarding revision in Maximum Retail Price (MRP) of Rail Neer (1000 ml and 500 ml) bottles pursuant to reduction in GST on Packaged Drinking Water (PDW) from 18% to 5%. Sir/ Madam, Pursuant to Regulation 30 of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, this is to inform that consequent to the reduction in Goods and Services Tax (GST) on Packaged Drinking Water (PDW) from 18% to 5%, the Ministry of Railways, Government of India, has approved the revision in the Maximum Retail Price (MRP) of Rail Neer bottles, as tabled below: Pack Size Existing MRP (₹) Revised MRP (₹) Effective Date 1000 ml ₹15 ₹14 22 nd September, 2025 500 ml ₹10 ₹9 22 nd September, 2025 The above revision is in line with the directives of the Government and to pass on the benefit of the reduced tax burden to railway passengers. This is for your information and record please.

text: Price revision aimed at strengthening reliability, service quality, and future-ready logistics solutions Mumbai, September 29, 2025: Allcargo Gati Limited, one of India’s premier Express Distribution and Supply Chain Management companies, has announced an average 10.2% General Price Increase (GPI) effective January 1, 2026, for its Express Distribution services. The revision reflects the need to balance rising operational costs while enabling continued investments in infrastructure, technology, and customer service excellence. Over the years, Allcargo Gati has consistently prioritized service quality through innovation and modernization. The company has introduced handheld printers for faster invoicing, improved Proof of Delivery (POD) accuracy using Machine Learning, and established a centralized Control Tower offering real-time, end-to-end shipment visibility.

text: Sub: Advance intimation regarding price increase In continuation to our earlier letter dated April 08, 2026 submitted in respect of price increase on Hyundai cars, considering the prevailing market conditions and to ensure balanced approach towards customer interest, we would like to inform that the new prices will now be made effective from June 01, 2026. The extent of price increase is up to a maximum of Rs. 12,800 /- and it will vary depending on the model and variant. The price increase has been necessitated due to rising input costs, increased commodity prices and higher operational expenses, amongst other reasons. While the company continuously strives to optimize costs and minimize the impact on its customers, the company is constrained to pass on some of the increased costs to the market through this nominal price increase. We request you to take this on record.

text: Subject: Clarification letter Re: Your email dated June 2, 2025, regarding Clarification for Financial results - INFY We wish to inform you that, t he clause being referred is under Reg 33 (3)(e) is replicated below for reference: The listed entity shall also submit the audited or limited reviewed financial results in respect of the last quarter along-with the results for the entire financial year, with a note stating that the figures of last quarter are the balancing figures between audited figures in respect of the full financial year and the published year-to-date figures upto the third quarter of the current financial year Our response – As per the SEBI clause a note has to be given stating that the last quarter figures (Q4) is the balancing figure of year to date figures for the full year and the figures published till Q3 of that year.

text: Sub: Update - Sub-division of Equity Shares We refer to our intimations dated November 21, 2025 and December 27, 2025 in connection with the sub-division of equity shares of Rs. 5/- each of Kotak Mahindra Bank Limited (“Bank”). text: Sub: Disclosure under Regulation 30 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 The Company has received an order dated November 6, 2025 (“Order”) from the Commissioner (Appeals), Central Goods and Services Tax, Appeal Commissionerate – Ahmedabad imposing on the Company a penalty of Rs. 57.07 crore under Section 74 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 and applicable provisions of the Integrated Goods and Services Act, 2017. The Order has been passed on the basis that the Company has paid a lesser amount of tax due to the classification adopted for import of service related to hiring of vessels on time charter basis during the period from July 1, 2017 to January 24, 2018. The Company intends to file an appeal against the Order. The financial impact of the Order is to the extent of the penalty levied.

text: Sub: Intimation under Regulation 30 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 – Receipt of Notice of Strike Pursuant to Regulation 30 of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, we inform you that a strike notice has been issued by the Workers’ Union to take effect on or after September 3, 2025, demanding reinstatement of four dismissed workmen and a few who are under suspension. The dismissals were carried out after the charges of serious misconduct were proved through extensive enquiry processes and those under suspension are undergoing lawful enquiry processes for serious misconduct. As such, the call for a strike is considered inappropriate. The Company is in the process of applying for an injunction order in this regard and is taking all necessary measures to resolve the matter and ensure uninterrupted operations. Further updates will be provided in due course.

text: Subject: Update on temporary disruption of o perations at Kassar Plant, Bahadurgarh, Haryana In continuation of our earlier intimation dated 17th August, 2025, regarding the temporary disruption of operations at the Kassar Plant, Bahadurgarh, Haryana (“Plant”), we wish to provide the following update pursuant to Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015: The supply of natural gas to the Plant, which was earlier fully disrupted on a temporary basis due to the incident in GAIL’s Gauna - Bawana pipeline, has now been partially restored. Accordingly, the operations at the Plant have been resumed in part. The Company is in the process of assessing other options for mitigating the disruption and to gradually scale up the production. All other manufacturing locations of the Company remain fully operational.

text: Sub: Disclosure under Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations & Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 – Disruption of operations at our Roorkee plant due to natural calamity (floods) Pursuant to Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, we wish to inform you that operations at our manufacturing unit located in Roorkee, Uttarakhand, have been disrupted today due to heavy rains and flooding in the region. text: New Delhi, India – January 29th, 2026: Shivalik Bimetal Controls Limited (SBCL) confirmed a minor fire incident at its main manufacturing facility in the packaging area between 10:15 and 10:2 5 PM on 28th January 2026. In-house fire-fighting and local fire authorities responded promptly, and the fire has been fully extinguished. There were no casualties, and no damage to machinery or production equipment. The incident caused minimal damage limited to the packing area. Management Commentary: Mr. Kabir Ghumman, Managing Director, said: “Safety is our top priority at Shivalik, and in any such incident our first concern is always the well - being of our people. The fire was limited to the packaging area and was controlled quickly by our in - house fire-fighting team, with timely support from the local fire authorities. The cause of the fire is under investigation.

text: Sub: Disclosure under SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 ("Listing Regulations") This is to inform that a fire incident occurred at one of the manufacturing facilities of our supplier i.e. Mobis India Limited (“Mobis”) at Irrungattukottai, Kancheepuram District of Tamil Nadu in the late afternoon of May 31, 2026. No fatality has been reported. The above facility of Mobis supplies audio components and few other automotive parts to the Company. The Company and Mobis teams are working closely to assess the situation and extent of damage to Mobis facility. This incident will result in temporary disruption to Company's production. However, alternative sourcing and supply continuity measures are being actively explored to minimize the operational impact. There is sufficient vehicle inventory in our dealer network to take care of the customer demand.

We wish to inform you that the Company has today commenced commercial production of VAE at its VAE manufacturing facility in Dahej, Gujarat, having an installed capacity of 1,50,000 tons per annum. The VAE manufactured at the facility is intended to be primarily utilised for captive consumption at the Company’s paint manufacturing facilities.
